Welcome 👋

This interactive guide covers CSE433 Deep Learning, Lectures 1–5 of CMU's 11-785 (Bhiksha Raj): what a neuron computes, why networks need depth, what a network can represent, how it learns (perceptron, ADALINE, empirical risk), the calculus of optimisation, losses, and backpropagation. It also works every problem of Sheet 1 and Assignment 3, and every class poll. Every number in it was computed by code, and where the slides contain a mistake, the guide says so and gives the correct version. Navigate through the modes below:

  • 📖 Tutorial Mode: each step goes idea → worked example → why → quick check, with tap-to-trace tables and eight hands-on labs (gates, K-maps, regions, staircases, the perceptron algorithm, gradient descent, softmax, backprop).
  • 🎴 Flash Cards: definitions, weights, formulas and numbers to know cold.
  • 🎯 Professor's Focus: Part 1 (Lectures 1–2 + Sheet 1) and Part 2 (Lectures 3–5 + Assignment 3), every problem worked in full.
  • ⚡ Practice Quiz: exam-style MCQs for every topic, including every class poll from the slides (the weekly quizzes reuse them).

💡 Short on time? Do Tutorials 4, 7, 10 and 11: Boolean MLPs, the perceptron algorithm, losses, and backprop hold most of the numbers. Press Ctrl+K to search, and open the 📋 Cheat Sheet (bottom-right) for every formula.

📋 Exam Reference Sheet

History (Lecture 1)

  • Associationism (Aristotle's 4 laws: contiguity, frequency, similarity, contrast) → connectionism: knowledge is in the connections. First proposed by Alexander Bain (1873). Brain ≈ 80 billion neurons, ≈ 100 trillion connections.
  • McCulloch & Pitts (1943): neurons as Boolean logic; inhibitory synapse vetoes firing; no learning rule.
  • Hebb (1949): w_xy ← w_xy + η·x·y. "Fire together, wire together". Unstable: weights only grow (no reduction, no competition). Fix: Sanger's rule w_ij ← w_ij + η·y_j(x_i − Σ_{k≤j} w_ik y_k).
  • Rosenblatt (1958) perceptron: w ← w + η(d − y)x, provably convergent for linearly separable classes. Minsky & Papert (1969): one unit can't do XOR.
  • Turing (1948): A-type = random NAND nets (no learning); B-type = connections with learnable "modifiers".

The threshold unit

  • z = Σ wᵢxᵢ + b, y = H(z) = 1 if z ≥ 0 else 0, with b = −T (T = threshold). Fires iff Σwᵢxᵢ ≥ T.
  • Linear: 3x + 7y (no constant). Affine: linear + constant, 3x + 7y + 4. (Every linear function is also affine.)
  • AND: w = (1, 1), T = 2 · OR: (1, 1), T = 1 · NOT: w = −1, T = 0 · NAND: (−1, −1), T = −1.
  • Universal AND (X₁…X_L plain, X_{L+1}…X_N negated): weights +1/−1, T = L. Universal OR: T = L − N + 1. At least K of the desired polarity: T = L − N + K.
  • A single unit is a linear classifier: boundary w·x + b = 0, w points to the side that fires.

XOR and depth

  • No single unit computes XOR (needs w₁ ≥ T, w₂ ≥ T, T > 0, w₁ + w₂ < T: contradiction).
  • 3 units: h₁ = OR (1, 1, T = 1), h₂ = NAND (−1, −1, T = −1), out = AND (1, 1, T = 2).
  • 2 units (skip connections): h = AND(x, y) (T = 2); out: x·1 + y·1 + h·(−2) ≥ 1.
  • Depth = longest path from a source (input) to a sink (output). "Deep" = depth > 2 (≥ 3 layers). Layer = all neurons at the same depth.

Boolean functions as MLPs (Lecture 2)

  • Any truth table → DNF (one AND term per 1-row) → one hidden layer of AND units + an OR output. So one hidden layer is a universal Boolean function.
  • K-map grouping reduces the DNF → fewer hidden units (L2 p47: 7 terms → 3: ȲZ̄ + W̄XȲ + X̄YZ̄).
  • Worst case (checkerboard = parity, nothing groups): 2^(N−1) hidden units, 2^(N−1) + 1 in all. N = 10 → 512.
  • Deep XOR network: 3(N − 1) perceptrons (2(N − 1) with the 2-unit XOR), arranged in 2 log₂N layers (pairing tree).
  • Only K hidden layers: O(2^(CN)) neurons in the K-th layer, C = 2^(−(K−1)/2).
  • Parity ∉ AC⁰: a depth-d AND/OR circuit needs size ≈ 2^(n^(1/d)). Shannon: almost all n-input functions need > 2ⁿ/n gates whatever the depth.
  • Threshold circuits: parity in depth 2 with O(n²) weights, depth log n with O(n). Parameters = number of connections.

Decision regions

  • Convex polygon with N edges = N edge units + AND (Σyᵢ ≥ N). Hexagon: 7 units. Region sums: N inside, N−1 past one edge, N−2 past two…
  • Non-convex / disjoint regions: AND each convex piece, OR the pieces → 2 hidden layers.
  • One hidden layer is enough in the limit: many-sided polygon ≈ circle with Σ = N inside, N/2 outside; bias −N/2 → N/2 inside, 0 outside; fill any shape with circles (K → ∞). MLPs are universal classifiers.
  • Σyᵢ = N(1 − (1/π) arccos(min(1, r/|x − c|))).
  • Depth helps: 16-line grid → 56 hidden (16 + 40) with 2 layers, 61 as an XOR tree (46 with 2-unit XOR); 64 lines → 608 (64 + 544) vs 253 (190). Second layer ⌊(N+2)²/8⌋.

Real-valued functions

  • Pulse: H(x − T₁) − H(x − T₂) is 1 on [T₁, T₂). Sum scaled pulses → any 1-D function; cylinders → any N-D function. Universal approximator (one hidden layer, linear/summing output).
  • Staircase for x² on [0, 1]: cⱼ = (2j − 1)/K², error ≤ (2K − 1)/K² < 2/K; K = 200 for 10⁻².
  • Approximation ≠ exact representation. Output activation fixes the range: threshold {0,1}, sigmoid (0,1), tanh (−1,1), ReLU [0,∞), softplus (0,∞).
  • Every layer must be wide enough: < 16 threshold units can't capture the 16-line pattern; graded activations (ReLU) pass more information so narrow layers + depth can compensate.
  • VC dimension: threshold nets ∝ number of weights; piecewise-linear ∝ (weights)².

Learning (Lecture 3)

  • Learning = choosing W so f(X; W) ≈ g(X). True risk E[div(f(X; W), g(X))] needs g everywhere → use samples: empirical risk Loss(W) = (1/N) Σ div(f(Xᵢ; W), dᵢ). ERM: Ŵ = argmin Loss.
  • Perceptron algorithm (±1 labels): if sign(Wᵀxᵢ) ≠ yᵢ then W ← W + yᵢxᵢ. Converges after ≤ (R/γ)² mistakes for separable data (W₀ = 0; R = longest x; γ = margin). Never converges if not separable.
  • Augment: x̃ = [x, 1], w̃ = [w, b] → boundary through the origin of the bigger space; W ⊥ boundary, points to the + class.
  • MLP with threshold units can't be trained by the perceptron rule: hidden targets unknown → exponential relabelling search.
  • ADALINE: δ = d − z (before the threshold); w ← w + ηδx (delta / LMS rule) = gradient step on ½(d − z)². Perceptron: δ = d − y.
  • Generalized delta rule: δ = d − y, w ← w + ηδ f′(z) x (Widrow–Hoff).
  • MADALINE: on error, flip the hidden unit whose z is closest to 0; keep the flip if the error drops and ADALINE-train that unit toward it. Greedy, small nets only.
  • Threshold units: zero derivative almost everywhere → no direction to move. Fix: differentiable activation + differentiable divergence. Sigmoid output = P(Y = 1 | X) (logistic regression).

Derivatives (Lecture 4)

  • Δy ≈ f′(x)Δx. Scalar of vector: Δy = ∇ₓy Δx with ∇ₓy a 1 × N row; the gradient is its transpose (column).
  • Gradient = direction of fastest increase; −gradient = fastest decrease; ⊥ to level curves; 0 at optima.
  • Min of f(x): f′ = 0 and f″ > 0 (sufficient). Multivariate: ∇f = 0 and Hessian positive definite (all eigenvalues > 0).
  • Example: f = x₁² + x₁(1 − x₂) + x₂² − x₂x₃ + x₃² + x₃ → minimum at (−1, −1, −1), Hessian eigenvalues 2 − √2, 2, 2 + √2.

Gradient descent

  • x_{k+1} = x_k − η_k ∇f(x_k)ᵀ (ascent: +). Stop when |f(x_{k+1}) − f(x_k)| < ε₁ or ‖∇f‖ < ε₂.
  • Convex (bowl) + suitable η → global min. Non-convex → local min or inflection point.
  • Training: W ← W − η ∇Loss(W)ᵀ, Loss = (1/T) Σ Div(Yₜ, dₜ).

Activations and derivatives

  • sigmoid σ(z) = 1/(1 + e^−z), σ′ = σ(1 − σ) · tanh′ = 1 − tanh² · ReLU′ = 1 (z ≥ 0), 0 (z < 0) · softplus log(1 + e^z), ′ = σ(z).
  • Softmax yᵢ = e^zᵢ / Σⱼ e^zⱼ (a vector activation): ∂yⱼ/∂zᵢ = yᵢ(δᵢⱼ − yⱼ).

Outputs and divergences

  • Real outputs: L2 Div = ½‖Y − d‖², ∂/∂yᵢ = yᵢ − dᵢ.
  • Binary (sigmoid): Div = −d log Y − (1 − d) log(1 − Y); ∂/∂Y = −1/Y (d = 1), 1/(1 − Y) (d = 0). Not 0 at the minimum.
  • Multi-class (softmax, one-hot d): KL = Σ dᵢ log(dᵢ/yᵢ) = −log y_c; ∂/∂y_c = −1/y_c, 0 elsewhere.
  • Xent = −Σ dᵢ log yᵢ = KL + H(d) (slide p95 writes −H(d): sign slip); equal for one-hot.
  • Label smoothing: target 1 − (K − 1)ε at the class, ε elsewhere.
  • Softmax + KL, or linear + L2: ∇_z Div = (y − d)ᵀ.

Scalar backprop (Lecture 5)

  • Chain rule: dy/dx = Σᵢ (∂y/∂zᵢ)(dzᵢ/dx), summed over every path (influence diagram).
  • Forward: z_j⁽ᵏ⁾ = Σᵢ w_ij⁽ᵏ⁾ yᵢ⁽ᵏ⁻¹⁾ (y₀ = 1 for the bias), y_j⁽ᵏ⁾ = f_k(z_j⁽ᵏ⁾). Store everything.
  • Output: ∂Div/∂yᵢ⁽ᴺ⁾ = ∂Div(Y, d)/∂yᵢ; ∂Div/∂zᵢ = f′(zᵢ) ∂Div/∂yᵢ.
  • Weights: ∂Div/∂w_ij⁽ᵏ⁾ = yᵢ⁽ᵏ⁻¹⁾ · ∂Div/∂z_j⁽ᵏ⁾ (bias: input 1).
  • Down one layer: ∂Div/∂yᵢ⁽ᵏ⁻¹⁾ = Σⱼ w_ij⁽ᵏ⁾ ∂Div/∂z_j⁽ᵏ⁾.
  • Vector activation: ∂Div/∂zᵢ = Σⱼ (∂Div/∂yⱼ)(∂yⱼ/∂zᵢ). Max: 1 for the argmax, 0 else. ReLU at 0: any subgradient in [0, 1].
  • Backprop computes the derivatives; gradient descent uses them to train.

Vector form

  • z_k = W_k y_{k−1} + b_k, y_k = f_k(z_k); W_k is D_k × D_{k−1}.
  • Jacobian J_y(z) = [∂yᵢ/∂zⱼ] (diagonal for scalar activations). Chain rule: outer derivative first, ∇ₓy = ∇_z y ∇ₓz.
  • For z = Wy + b: ∇_y D = ∇_z D · W, ∇_W D = y · ∇_z D, ∇_b D = ∇_z D (shapes are transposes of W and b).
  • Backward loop k = N…1: ∇_{z_k} = ∇_{y_k} J_{y_k}(z_k); ∇_{y_{k−1}} = ∇_{z_k} W_k; ∇_{W_k} = y_{k−1}∇_{z_k}; ∇_{b_k} = ∇_{z_k}.
  • Update: W_k ← W_k − (η/T)(∇_{W_k}Loss)ᵀ, b_k ← b_k − (η/T)(∇_{b_k}Loss)ᵀ (p195 wrongly reuses ∇W).

Final answers (each one is worked in the tutorials and Professor's Focus)

  • Sheet 1 P1: w = (1, −1, 1, −1, 1, −1), b = −1 (threshold 1 = L − N + K = 3 − 6 + 4)
  • Sheet 1 P2: no single unit (w₁ ≥ T, w₂ ≥ T, T > 0 vs w₁ + w₂ < T); 2 hidden: OR (1, 1, b = −1) and NAND (−1, −1, b = 1), output AND (1, 1, b = −2)
  • Sheet 1 P3: DNF: 2^(N−1) = 128 hidden units for N = 8; tree: 7 XOR modules, 14 hidden units inside them, 3 stages; O(N) modules
  • Sheet 1 P4: F = x̄₂x̄₄ + x₂x₄ (XNOR of x₂, x₄): 8 hidden units → 2
  • Sheet 1 P5: 4 rectangles [−2,2]×[−2,−1], [−2,2]×[0,1], [−2,−1]×[−1,0], [1,2]×[−1,0]; 16 half-space units + 4 AND + 1 OR
  • Sheet 1 P6: c₀ = 0, cⱼ = (2j − 1)/K²; error ≤ (2K − 1)/K² < 2/K; K = 200; approximation only, not exact
  • Sheet 1 P7: (a) T (b) F (c) F (d) T (e) F (f) F
  • Assignment 3 P1: one update (sample 1, pass 1) → w̃ = [2, 1, 1]; boundary 2x₁ + x₂ + 1 = 0; R = √6 ≈ 2.4495
  • Assignment 3 P2: z = 0.8, y = 1, δ_P = 0, δ_A = 0.2; perceptron unchanged, ADALINE → [0.34, −0.42, −0.18]
  • Assignment 3 P3: unit 2 (|z| = 0.15); output 1 → 0; w₂ ← w₂ + η(d₂ − w₂ᵀx)x
  • Assignment 3 P4: w* = Σxd / Σx² = 30.2 / 30 ≈ 1.0067
  • L4 p35–37 example: minimum at (−1, −1, −1), f = −1, Hessian eigenvalues 0.586, 2, 3.414
